title: Who were the first Americans?
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss the first Americans: why Columbus is not the discoverer of the Americas (Norse, a legendary Irish monk, and claims of Chinese voyages), the old spontaneous generation theory and Pasteur's disproof, the 1908 Clovis-area discoveries in New Mexico, radiocarbon dating showing Clovis age (about 11,000 years), the Clovis First theory and the "Clovis police," the Bering Land Bridge migration hypothesis, the Pleistocene overkill hypothesis, the Younger Dryas impact hypothesis, Tom Dillehay's Monte Verde site in Chile (about 12,500 years old, with later evidence near 33,000 years), and Australia as a comparison. The episode closes with a Kiva.org fundraising team announcement and a listener letter from Chris, who lives on a commune.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter, then ask who discovered America, noting that Columbus was preceded by the Norse and a legendary Irish monk, and that Chinese voyage claims are disputed.

segments.title: Spontaneous generation and the question of where people came from
segments.summary: Josh explains that once Europeans realized the continents were new, the question became where the Native Americans came from. He describes the spontaneous generation theory and says Louis Pasteur disproved it in 1864.

segments.title: Discovery of Clovis points near Clovis, New Mexico
segments.summary: A 1908 flood in southern New Mexico exposed unusual spearheads near Clovis. Ridgely Whiteman later found one in bison bones, and a New Mexico highway excavation turned up more finds. A dispute over moved spear points is described, and in 1932 the finds were recognized as very old.

segments.title: Radiocarbon dating and the Clovis First theory
segments.summary: Radiocarbon dating in the 1950s dated the Clovis site to about 11,200 years ago, which supported the view that Clovis were the first Americans. The hosts describe the Clovis-first establishment, the Bering Land Bridge crossing, the hafted big-game hunting, and the Pleistocene overkill idea.

segments.title: Clovis mystery and the Younger Dryas impact theory
segments.summary: The hosts note that Clovis tools appear and vanish suddenly and that no earlier technology precedes them. They describe the Younger Dryas comet impact hypothesis, which was later challenged.

segments.title: Monte Verde in Chile and other migration theories
segments.summary: Tom Dillehay's work at Monte Verde in Chile found wood with knotted strings and mastodon flesh dated to about 12,500 years ago, which predates Clovis. The hosts discuss the missing settlements along the migration route, the Australia comparison, and a later site dated to about 33,000 years.

segments.title: Relevance of archaeology and closing comments
segments.summary: The hosts discuss whether the topic matters to listeners today and conclude that archaeology's value is mainly in pursuing the truth.

segments.title: Kiva.org team announcement
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck announce a Stuff You Should Know team on Kiva.org for micro loans, with a $25 minimum donation, and encourage listeners to join.
topics: Stuff You Should Know Kiva team

segments.title: Listener mail: Chris on commune living
segments.summary: A listener named Chris writes about living on a commune with his wife on a yearly income under ten thousand dollars, in response to a request about leaving the rat race.
